| [THEORY-032](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-032.md) | Yoneda presupposes the relata | nLab, Yoneda lemma (rev. 2026-08-17), [LIT-221](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-221.md) — y is fully faithful and y(c) ≅ y(d) iff c ≅ d, and pointwise bijections of hom-sets without naturality do not suffice. Lam & Wüthrich ([LIT-222](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-222.md)) state two of its consequences without the name. The philosophical reading, a relational criterion of identity up to isomorphism rather than a construction of objects from relations, is the record's own. It does not say that the lemma supports eliminating objects. | Active |
| [THEORY-038](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-038.md) | Category theory gives radical OSR no support | Lam & Wüthrich (2015), [LIT-222](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-222.md), against Bain (2013), [LIT-223](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-223.md). Bain's "structure as object in a category" relabels relata rather than removing them, and his GR and TQFT cases dispose of points only. That the Yoneda lemma ([LIT-221](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-221.md)) strengthens the rebuttal is the record's inference: no paper in the debate names it. This does not refute radical OSR. It removes one argument for it, and Eva 2016's reply is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-401](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-401.md) | Numerosity gives a fair lottery on ℕ | Wenmackers (2011), [LIT-163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-163.md), chapter 2, read in [NOTE-139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md). P_num(A) = num(A)/α is defined on all of 𝒫(ℕ), gives each ticket 1/α > 0, and satisfies FAIR, ALL and a hypercountable form of SUM (eqs. 2.20–2.27). Proved, given the axiom of choice. It is not a free lunch: one solution per free ultrafilter, no invariance under relabelling, no countable additivity, and by the author's own admission it is empirically indistinguishable from the finitely additive real-valued solution. | Active |
| [THEORY-604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md) v2 | Most dualities are adjunctions to an opposite | Corfield (2017), [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md), read in [NOTE-141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md). A short programmatic paper. That most dualities of interest are covered by constructions around adjunction is shown by worked exposition of standard cases, not proved. There is unlikely to be "a single monolithic account" (pp. 59–60). Reserving "duality" for structural reversal is a stated preference, and the verdicts on string dualities are a paragraph each. The proposal that philosophers of physics need homotopy type theory is an expectation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-729](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-729.md) | Adjunctions restrict to dual equivalences | Corfield (2017), [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md), §3, read in full in [NOTE-141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md), with the proof the paper omits written out here. For F : C → D^op left adjoint to G : D^op → C, let C′ and D′ be the full subcategories on which the unit and the counit are isomorphisms. Then F and G restrict to inverse equivalences C′ ≃ D′, and D′ is a full subcategory of D^op, so C′ is dually equivalent to a full subcategory of D. Pontrjagin duality is the example. That most dualities are of this form is [THEORY-604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md)'s thesis, still Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-2307](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2307.md) | Assertion is of judgements; propositions are sets | Martin-Löf (1984), [LIT-3232](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3232.md), read in [NOTE-2419](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2419.md) for [LEAD-215](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-215.md) from a course-hosted scan, Skimmed. The source of the propositions-as-sets reading and of the table that reads an element as a program "which meets the specification A" (p. 6). It does not bear on the direction of fit as inference against checking. Proposed until a model shows the meaning explanations consistent. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2308](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2308.md) | Intuitionistic logic is a calculus of problems | Kolmogorov (1932), [LIT-3229](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-3229.md), read in [NOTE-2422](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2422.md) from the GDZ scan. A problem is explained by examples (p. 59), is solved and not true (p. 61, n. 8), and, fully stated, carries its permitted means (p. 59, n. 2); a ⊃ b reduces b's solution to a's, ¬a derives a contradiction from a supposed solution of a. The calculus coincides in form with Heyting's (pp. 58, 63) and does not solve a ∨ ¬a. §2: an existence statement is a problem plus its solution, and a problem's sense is independent of the state of our knowledge (p. 65). It corroborates [CLAIM-949](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md)'s correspondence of a question with a problem, narrowed ([ARG-245](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-245.md)), and corrects its attribution: Kolmogorov keeps statements and problems apart. The wording is the filer's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
